content: Topical antibiotics are medications applied directly to the skin to treat acne. They work by reducing the population of Cutibacterium acnes (C. acnes), the bacteria associated with acne development. These antibiotics also help decrease inflammation in the affected areas. Commonly used topical antibiotics for acne include clindamycin and erythromycin. They are often prescribed in combination with other treatments, such as benzoyl peroxide, to enhance efficacy and reduce the risk of bacterial resistance. Prolonged use of topical antibiotics alone is generally discouraged due to the potential for antibiotic resistance. Patients should apply these medications as directed by their healthcare provider to achieve optimal results and minimize side effects.
